guardian.description:
Drive to save thousands of Afrikaners from false claims of ‘white genocide’ appears to show signs of slowing

When Donald Trump announced in February 2025 that the US would accept Afrikaners from South Africa as refugees, many white South Africans who believed that they were victims of racism in their country thought that their prayers had been answered.

guardian.description:
Almost 3,500 people have died in outbreak and experts say more must be done to ensure Bundibugyo is under control

Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak.

For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the numbers of people becoming infected is slowing down, according to officials.

Inside the Great Hall of St Bartholomew’s North Wing, alongside stately portraits of the apostle from whom London’s oldest hospital takes its name and King Henry VIII, extravagant commemorative boards adorn the walls.

Public offering of Aliko Dangote’s Nigerian oil refinery business could swell his net wealth by two-thirds

The fortune of Africa’s richest person could swell by two thirds to nearly $60bn (£44bn) after his refinery in Nigeria listed publicly in the continent’s biggest-ever initial public offering.

If Monday’s flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals on the Nigerian exchange goes to plan, then Aliko Dangote will add a further $23bn (£17bn) to his $35bn net worth.<

Royal guards carry casket through streets of Fort Portal amid row over appointment of Edward Rukidi Kijanangoma

Uganda’s King Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, long the world’s youngest monarch, has been buried among the tombs of his royal forebears as ⁠his Tooro kingdom looked to put ⁠a bitter succession battle behind ​it.

guardian.description:
Latest daily reductions will further choke one of the world’s most important shipping lanes

The Panama canal plans to again cut maritime traffic due to worsening drought caused by the El Niño climate phenomenon, further choking up one of the world’s most important shipping lanes.

guardian.description:
Neck-and-neck with Lula in polls, Flávio Bolsonaro fires up his base in the bellwether state of Minas Gerais – starting at the scene of his father’s stabbing

A giant banner of Brazil’s incarcerated former president Jair Bolsonaro fluttered in the morning breeze as his eldest son, Flávio, touched down at an airfield on the fringe of a city that will soon help decide the future of one of the biggest democracies on earth.

“Brazil is rudderless. Brazil has no president and Brazil need

guardian.description:
Canadian PM Mark Carney hosts president in Calgary, where he grew up alongside large Ukrainian community

Canada offered support on Thursday to boost Ukraine’s air defenses and help replenish its drone stocks, as the countries pledged to deepen their alliance during a visit by Volodymyr Zelenskyy.

Mark Carney hosted the president of Ukraine in Calgary in the western province of Alberta, where the Canadian prime minister grew up among a large community of people with Ukrainian herit

guardian.description:
Rubio visits Ecuador and welcomes cooperation after campaign of unilateral strikes on alleged ‘narco-terrorists’

The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, gave new clarity on the approach toward combating drug trafficking in Latin American waters, saying the Trump administration was focused on working with allied countries and aligning with their laws but insisted the military would “still blow up ships if need be”.

guardian.description:
Trump administration to seek extra funding from Congress to ‘dismantle’ Los Tiguerones over narcotics trafficking

The US has designated Ecuador’s Los Tiguerones gang, which stormed a television station during a live broadcast in 2024, as a terrorist organisation as the Trump administration expands its campaign against narcotics traffickers it says are destabilising Latin America.

Donald Trump dismisses attempts to increase controls on artificial intelligence as ‘sick conspiracy’

guardian.description:
Police in Bali believe the two young children died as a result of violence, while a 57-year-old man is believed to have taken his own life

Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.

The man, 57, and his two children, seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday m

guardian.title: At least six dead and 130 missing after Indonesian ferry capsizes, officials say
guardian.description:
Search and rescue agency says 107 people brought to safety from vessel hit by bad weather in Java Sea

Rescue workers in Indonesia said at least six people had died and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo capsized in bad weather.

Basarnas, Indonesia’s national search and rescue agency, said 107 people had been rescued from the Virgo ⁠Transport 8 vessel, which set sail on Saturday with 243 ​people onboard, including 30 crew

guardian.title: One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas
guardian.description:
Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continue

One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu, the country’s government says.

The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive.

guardian.title: Xi Jinping gets red carpet at Brics summit amid thaw in India-China relations
guardian.description:
Chinese president’s arrival in Delhi seen as step towards reconciliation after deadly 2020 military clash

The Chinese president, Xi Jinping, has received a red-carpet welcome in India for a summit of Brics developing nations, as regional rivals Beijing and Delhi make a public display of thawing relations while quietly competing to lead at a time of shaky US global dominance.

As Xi stepped off the plane, he was walked past an honour guard of Indian soldiers and traditional dancers

bbc.description: DHS inspectors say they found the immigration-detention centre violated basic standards for hygiene, medical care, food and safety.

bbc.description: A nationwide appeal was launched after Elizabeth Moselakgomo went missing last week. Four other women's bodies have been found nearby.

bbc.description: At least 12 people are being treated for anthrax after eating infected meat from wildlife carcasses.

euronews.title: US Supreme Court deals blow to Trump's attempts to restrict mail ballots ahead of midterm election
euronews.description: The decision allows states to continue sending out mail ballots under the same processes they’ve used for years and have accounted for nearly a third of votes cast.

euronews.description: Reading for pleasure isn't just enjoyable, new research suggests it could also boost brain health and lower dementia risk.

euronews.description: The war in Ukraine, enlargement, migration, climate and trade are all expected to feature in Brussels’ most eagerly awaited speech of the year — with the possibility of a surprise announcement always lurking around the corner.

euronews.description: Ursula von der Leyen slammed fossil fuels in her 2022 State of the EU speech. Now, Europe is in the midst of yet another energy crisis.

euronews.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this September 15th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

euronews.title: Canada is eyeing a ‘unique alliance’ with the EU. How far can Brussels go?
euronews.description: President Trump’s tariff war and territorial threats have made Ottawa pivot towards Europe. Brussels now wants to seize the political moment and draw Canada deeper into its orbit.

euronews.title: Revealed: The world's best destinations for a last-minute holiday – with plenty in Europe
euronews.description: Not one for planning months ahead? New research has revealed where travellers are most likely to book accommodation within a week of arrival, with four European countries making the global top 10.

euronews.title: Germany seeks guarantees from Italy's UniCredit over Commerzbank takeover
euronews.description: Berlin seeks guarantees from UniCredit as its leverage over Commerzbank fades and the Italian lender moves closer to taking control.

euronews.title: Maduro ally Alex Saab expected to plead guilty in federal money laundering case
euronews.description: Charged with a single count of money laundering tied to an alleged conspiracy to create fake companies and falsify shipping records, Saab is scheduled to appear before Judge in Miami on Tuesday for a change of plea hearing, according to court records.

euronews.title: Trillions sitting idle: Here's how much money Europeans are losing on savings
euronews.description: Europeans are losing an average of €294 in purchasing power for every €10,000 they keep in the bank, according to a study from Revolut, which found €6.3 trillion sitting in low-yield deposits across 20 EU countries at a moment when Brussels is trying to push that money into capital markets.

euronews.title: United States Space Force says US has weapons in orbit
euronews.description: Once a hunting ground for Cold War bragging rights, space has now evolved into a key strategic arena, as states jostle for a military and technological edge.

euronews.title: Finland joins France's forward nuclear deterrence initiative
euronews.description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb stressed that Finland’s "foremost priority" was still to act as part of NATO and the EU and that the French initiative would not "replace or overlap with NATO’s nuclear deterrence."

euronews.title: Former Moroccan spy reportedly offered Spain intelligence information in bid to avoid extradition
euronews.description: Mehdi Hijaouy was reportedly forced into exile following a conflict with some of his intelligence colleagues in Morocco.

euronews.title: France seeks Usmanov delisting in bid to secure release of French nationals detained in Azerbaijan
euronews.description: Paris seeks to remove Usmanov from the sanctions list in an apparent quid-pro-quo move to secure the release of detained French nationals.

euronews.title: Turkish Airlines drops Luanda as Angola's new airport struggles
euronews.description: The Istanbul carrier permanently axed Luanda, along with four other African routes, becoming the latest international airline to exit the Angolan capital since its new airport opened in 2023. The facility was built for 15 million annual passengers but handled fewer than 800,000 in 2025.

euronews.title: Italy and wolves: living with a growing population amid myths and alarmism
euronews.description: The latest data put Italy's wolf population at around 3,500 animals spread nationwide, and experts say it has since grown. Amid sightings and scares, what is being done and what must be known so farmers, residents and wolves can live side by side?

euronews.title: Iran seizes assets of 240 dissidents and journalists as protest arrests top 6,000
euronews.description: The judiciary froze 182 bank accounts and confiscated property belonging to journalists, activists and public figures accused of acting in favour of "hostile governments". Tehran has executed at least 532 people since January, including 29 linked to the protests.

euronews.title: Parliament pushes tougher energy permit deadlines, setting up clash with EU countries
euronews.description: The European Parliament is trying to turn permitting reform into a stronger, common EU rulebook, while capitals seek flexibility to accommodate national legal systems, environmental constraints and administrative structures, according to a document seen by Euronews.

lemonde.title: Flambée du pétrole et hausse des taux : nouvelle alerte sur les finances publiques françaises
lemonde.description: Le taux d’intérêt auquel la France doit s’endetter est monté à 4,5 %, lundi 14 septembre. Du jamais-vu depuis 2008. L’écart avec l’Allemagne, un pays jugé beaucoup plus fiable, a également atteint un nouveau record.

lemonde.title: Quand une banque chinoise soutient le nickel russe pendant la guerre en Ukraine
lemonde.description: Des documents confidentiels révèlent comment l’Industrial and Commercial Bank of China a courtisé des entreprises à haut risque, tel un géant russe du nickel, secteur frappé en 2024 par les sanctions occidentales, pour garantir des ressources et des alliances au régime de Xi Jinping.

lemonde.title: Climat : après un été de canicules et de sécheresse sans précédent, les militants écologistes espèrent remobiliser
lemonde.description: Des ONG et des syndicats appellent à un rassemblement, mardi, devant le ministère de l’économie et des finances, pour demander des mesures d’urgence climatiques. Le 26 septembre, 200 manifestations sont prévues à travers la France « pour le climat, le vivant, la paix et la justice sociale ».

lemonde.title: Donald Trump voit son projet de restriction du vote par correspondance rejeté par la Cour suprême, à six semaines des midterms
lemonde.description: Les juges n’ont pas statué sur le fond mais ont considéré, dans une décision rendue lundi, qu’une application aussi rapide de l’encadrement strict demandé par le président républicain aurait pu perturber le scrutin.

lemonde.title: Un homme d’affaires malien victime d’un spectaculaire cambriolage à un million d’euros dans un palace parisien
lemonde.description: Des voleurs se sont introduits, en escaladant la façade du Plaza Athénée, dans la chambre d’Oumar Gambi, un entrepreneur malien célèbre dans son pays et qui gravite dans l’entourage du président congolais Denis Sassou Nguesso.

lemonde.title: Aux Emmy Awards, la comédie horrifique « Widow’s Bay », grande favorite de la soirée, fait le plein de statuettes
lemonde.description: La cérémonie, qui s’est tenue lundi soir à Los Angeles, souvent présentée comme l’équivalent des Oscars de la télévision américaine, s’est achevée sur une pluie de records. « The Pitt » a été sacrée meilleure série dramatique.

lemonde.title: Marine Le Pen consolide son ancrage chez les retraités, son obsession en vue de la présidentielle de 2027
lemonde.description: Le RN s’oppose aux pistes d’économie du gouvernement pour marquer son soutien aux retraités, qui lui ont jusqu’ici barré l’accès à l’Elysée. Cette défense de leur pouvoir d’achat va de pair avec un affichage de sérieux.

lemonde.title: La pollution de l’air contribuerait à creuser les inégalités scolaires
lemonde.description: Une étude du Laboratoire sur les inégalités mondiales suggère que la pollution de l’air peut expliquer jusqu’à 25 % de l’écart de réussite aux examens entre les élèves issus de milieux socio-économiques défavorisés et ceux plus favorisés.

lemonde.title: Des migrants ont été enfermés dans des mini-cellules grillagées en Floride, une pratique « sans précédent » aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: Le centre de rétention, situé en Floride, a fonctionné pendant un an, entre début juillet 2025 et juin 2026, avant sa fermeture par la justice.

lemonde.title: Au Royaume-Uni, les millions perçus par le parti de Nigel Farage enflamment le débat sur le financement des formations politiques
lemonde.description: Les sommes très importantes reçues ces derniers jours par Reform UK ont provoqué un séisme dans le pays. Une loi visant à mieux encadrer de tels dons est en gestation.

lemonde.title: Dividendes : les grandes entreprises françaises ont versé le montant le plus élevé d’Europe au deuxième trimestre
lemonde.description: Les principales entreprises cotées dans l’Hexagone ont distribué 70,4 milliards de dollars à leurs actionnaires entre avril et juin, selon le gestionnaire d’actifs Janus Henderson. Le pays se place ainsi deuxième au niveau mondial, derrière les Etats-Unis.

lemonde.title: Les séries de la semaine : « Camarades », « Youth », « Slow Horses » et « Deadline »
lemonde.description: Chaque semaine, La Matinale propose une sélection de séries à découvrir sur petit écran. Cette semaine, notamment, retour en comédie sur l’après-1968.

lemonde.title: Le mariage du fils aîné de Donald Trump aux Bahamas sponsorisé par un homme d’affaires russe
lemonde.description: Le généreux contributeur, Umar Kremlev, un proche des cercles du pouvoir à Moscou, dirige la fédération controversée International Boxing Association et est aussi présent dans le secteur lucratif des paris sportifs en ligne.

lemonde.title: La fusée Vega-C s’envole de Kourou avec deux satellites européens
lemonde.description: Opéré par l’italien Avio, ce vol a pour mission de les mettre en orbite pour surveiller le climat et la santé des plantes depuis l’espace.

lemonde.title: Les Etats-Unis confirment disposer d’armes déployées en orbite
lemonde.description: Par cette déclaration, l’US Space Force officialise la militarisation de l’espace face à la Chine et la Russie.

lemonde.title: Vaccination contre la grippe : une couverture encore trop faible chez les personnes âgées et vulnérables en France, selon une étude
lemonde.description: Le rapport publié mardi par Santé publique France met en évidence de fortes disparités sociales et territoriales, avec des taux de vaccination plus faibles dans les outre-mer et le quart Sud-Est de l’Hexagone.

rfi.title: Environmental activists angry over controversial AI data centre near Paris
rfi.description: France is preparing to build Europe’s largest artificial intelligence data centre in a village outside of Paris. The government hopes to boost its computing infrastructure and give France an edge in the global race to develop AI, but activists are concerned about the impacts on health and the environment.

rfi.title: International justice 'can't be erased' despite US sanctions: ICC prosecutor
rfi.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) is facing US sanctions since deciding to issue arrest warrants over alleged war crimes in Gaza. Mame Mandiaye Niang, the Senegalese magistrate who has been acting head of the ICC's Office of the Prosecutor since his predecessor Karim Khan was forced out, tells RFI that while the Court's resilience is being tested, its existence is not under threat.

rfi.title: Finland joins French nuclear umbrella amid European security push
rfi.description: Finland has decided to join France’s nuclear deterrence umbrella in a bid to bolster regional security in the face of uncertainty over the United States' commitment to Europe and NATO.

rfi.title: France says Russia seeks to 'intimidate' EU with train attack near Poland
rfi.description: France and the European Union have condemned a Russian strike on a passenger train on the Polish border that has raised concerns about the risks of the war spreading closer to EU and NATO territory.

rfi.title: France seeks EU backing for revised social media ban for under-15s
rfi.description: A month after France’s Constitutional Council struck down a proposed social media ban for under-15s, the government has submitted a new version that President Emmanuel Macron wants passed before he leaves office in the spring.

rfi.title: World in Frames: RFI traces the stories behind the world's most famous photos
rfi.description: As France marks 200 years since inventor Nicéphore Niépce took the world’s oldest surviving photograph, RFI looks back at photos that changed our view of history – or even history itself. Here we tell the story of how a portrait of an unnamed woman came to represent the suffering of a nation in Dorothea Lange’s Migrant Mother, and what the iconic picture left out.

rfi.title: 'Historic day' for Nigeria as Dangote oil refinery launches IPO
rfi.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote on Monday launched what is slated as Africa's biggest initial public offering (IPO), which aims to raise $1.6 billion (€1.3 billion) to expand his mega oil refinery to become the world's largest.

rfi.title: Growing budgets show Africa keen to defend its place in the space race
rfi.description: African states invest around $500 million in space programmes annually, a figure expected to reach around $40 billion by 2030. With a number of initiatives already in place, the continent is seeking a seat at the table when it comes to international decisions on space exploration and equal access to the development of technology.

rfi.title: Normandy derailment inquiry widens focus on rail fragment found on track
rfi.description: A technical investigation has been launched into the derailment of a regional train near Rouen that left 44 people injured, as authorities work to establish how a piece of rail came to be lying on the track.

rfi.title: Sweden's election too close to call, left opposition narrowly leads
rfi.description: Sweden's general election is still too close to call, with Magdalena Andersson’s centre-left opposition coalition holding a narrow lead over Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s right-wing alliance.

rfi.title: Macron, Carney to visit French Atlantic islands with sovereignty message to Trump
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will visit the French North Atlantic territory of Saint-Pierre-and-Miquelon next week, in a symbolic show of support for national sovereignty amid renewed territorial claims by US President Donald Trump.

rfi.title: France moves to defuse US row over UN social media post
rfi.description: France has expressed regret over a social media post questioning the United States’ commitment to human rights, in a move expected to clear the way for its new ambassador to take up his post in Washington.

rfi.title: French Rafale jets take flight for 40,000-kilometre mission over three-continents
rfi.description: Four French Rafale fighter jets have embarked on a 40-day mission spanning three continents, highlighting France’s ability to deploy its air power around the world while strengthening cooperation with key international partners.

rfi.title: Radio France staff strike over appointment of right-wing magazine editor
rfi.description: Radio France staff began a two-day strike on Sunday over France Inter’s decision to hire a senior editor from the right-wing magazine Valeurs actuelles as a political commentator. Charles Sapin’s appointment has drawn criticism because the magazine has previously been convicted of racist public insult and incitement to racial hatred.

rfi.title: As catches dwindle, Congo River fishermen turn to plastic waste
rfi.description: On the Congo River, plastic is becoming the catch of the day. Some fishermen around Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, can now make more money pulling plastic from the water than catching fish, as declining catches and growing waste pollution threaten an artisanal way of life.

rfi.title: From townships to TikTok, South Africa's amapiano gets the world dancing
rfi.description: Amapiano dancers across South Africa are helping a sound born in the country's black townships reach audiences far beyond its borders – one viral challenge at a time. Short routines filmed in homes, schools and public spaces are spreading across social media, giving musicians another way to promote a genre that's now a global hit.

rfi.title: Erdogan hints at larger nuclear partnership with Russia, unsettling Turkey's allies
rfi.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is signalling a move to expand nuclear power cooperation with Russia, just as his country’s first Russian-built nuclear station prepares to go live later this year. The deepening partnership is likely to unsettle Turkey’s western allies.

rfi.title: Before its peak, El Nino brings failed crops and empty fishing nets
rfi.description: El Nino is already disrupting livelihoods and weather patterns around the world as one of the strongest events in decades continues to intensify. With its peak still months away, scientists warn the powerful Pacific climate phenomenon will bring more drought and flooding into 2027, while human-caused global warming is making some of its effects more severe.

france24fr.title: Olivier Grondeau, de l'enfer des prisons iraniennes à la première sélection du Goncourt
france24fr.description: Arrêté en Iran en 2022 et détenu pendant deux ans et demi, Olivier Grondeau raconte son expérience carcérale dans "Joseph dans la nuit" (L’Iconoclaste). Un récit nourri de ses rencontres en prison, qui figure dans la première sélection du prix Goncourt 2026.

france24fr.title: 🔴 En direct : le Pentagone reconnait une "pénurie" de munitions avec la guerre en Iran
Pourquoi les forces yéménites n’ont-elles pas réussi à stopper l’offensive des Houthis ?
france24fr.description: Les forces gouvernementales yéménites, pourtant soutenues militairement et financièrement par l’Arabie saoudite, ont cédé en quelques jours face à l’offensive des Houthis sur la côte de la mer Rouge. Une victoire qui est autant le produit de leur propre discipline que de la désunion persistante du camp gouvernemental.

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : des avions de chasse de l'Otan abattent un drone au-dessus de la Lituanie
france24fr.description: Un drone survolant la Lituanie a été détruit dans la nuit de lundi à mardi par des chasseurs de l'Otan, a annoncé le président lituanien. Selon la radio nationale lituanienne, le drone est venu de la Biélorussie voisine et se dirigeait vers l'Ouest.

france24fr.title: En direct : le Pentagone reconnait une "pénurie" de munitions avec la guerre en Iran
france24fr.description: Le ministère américain de la Défense a reconnu, dans un rapport publié lundi, une "pénurie" de munitions liée à la guerre en Iran, un constat que l'administration Trump avait pourtant largement refusé de confirmer ces derniers mois. Une série d'attaques menées par les Houthis du Yémen à l'aide de missiles balistiques et de drones a blessé 13 civils lundi dans le sud de l'Arabie saoudite, a annoncé mardi la coalition militaire dirigée par Riyad contre les rebelles pro-iraniens. Notre direct.

france24fr.title: La Cour suprême contrecarre les plans de Donald Trump sur le vote par correspondance
france24fr.description: Donald Trump a essuyé lundi un nouvel échec dans la bataille judiciaire autour du vote par correspondance aux États-Unis, à quelques semaines des élections de mi-mandat. La Cour suprême à majorité conservatrice a rejeté un recours de l'administration concernant un décret visant à encadrer davantage le vote postal.

france24fr.title: Les séries "Widow's Bay" et "The Pitt" triomphent aux Emmy Awards
france24fr.description: La comédie d'épouvante "Widow's Bay" a dominé la cérémonie des Emmy Awards lundi soir à Los Angeles, tandis que "The Pitt" a remporté pour la deuxième année consécutive le titre de meilleure série dramatique. La soirée a aussi vu Jean Smart décrocher un cinquième Emmy pour son rôle dans "Hacks".

france24fr.title: Invité par Washington, le Venezuela va participer au G20 consacré à l'énergie
france24fr.description: Caracas participe cette semaine à la réunion des ministres de l'Énergie du G20 à Houston, sur l'invitation des États-Unis, alors que Donald Trump cherche à revigorer l'exploitation des immenses réserves pétrolières du Venezuela.

france24fr.title: Houthis : les nouveaux maîtres de la mer Rouge ?
france24fr.description: En l’espace de quelques jours, à l’issue d’une offensive éclair, les insurgés houthis, pro-iraniens, ont pris le contrôle de l’ensemble du littoral yéménite de la mer Rouge. Déjà vendredi, il s'étaient emparés du stratégique détroit de Bab el-Mandeb. Autrefois simple guérilla de montagne, les insurgés d’Ansar Allah s'imposent de plus en plus sur la scène internationale.

france24fr.title: Espace : les États-Unis confirment pour la première fois avoir déployé des armes en orbite
france24fr.description: L'US Space Force a annoncé lundi posséder des "systèmes de contrôle spatial armés" capables de défendre les forces américaines contre des actions hostiles. Washington justifie ce déploiement par la montée en puissance de la Chine et de la Russie dans ce domaine.

france24fr.title: L'Ukraine se dit prête à des "mesures de désescalade" si la Russie en fait de même
france24fr.description: Le président ukrainien Volodymyr Zelensky a évoqué lundi une possible désescalade dans la guerre contre l'invasion russe, sans confirmer l'affirmation de Donald Trump selon laquelle Kiev et Moscou auraient accepté un arrêt mutuel des frappes sur les infrastructures énergétiques.

france24fr.title: Des fausses vidéos pour illustrer les frappes houthis en Arabie Saoudite
france24fr.description: En pleine offensive des Houthis contre l’Arabie Saoudite, une vidéo virale accrédite à tort l’idée d’une embuscade des rebelles contre les forces saoudiennes. De même, ces derniers jours, des images ont été présentées comme celles de dégâts qu'auraient occasionné des frappes yéménites sur des installations pétrolières saoudiennes.

france24fr.title: Mali : le Premier ministre algérien Sifi Ghrieb à Bamako pour relancer la coopération
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre algérien Sifi Ghrieb est arrivé lundi à Bamako pour une visite visant à consolider le rapprochement entre l'Algérie et le Mali, après plus d'un an de fortes tensions diplomatiques entre les deux voisins sahéliens. Cette visite intervient trois semaines après celle effectuée le 24 août par Abdoulaye Maïga à Alger. Le Premier ministre malien avait été reçu par le président algérien Abdelmadjid Tebboune et lui avait transmis un message du chef de la transition malienne.

france24fr.title: Le baril de pétrole à plus de 100 dollars alors que la tension monte au Moyen-Orient
france24fr.description: Les attaques de drones contre l'oléoduc est-ouest en Arabie saoudite et la prise de contrôle du détroit de Bab El -Manded par les rebelles houthistes du Yémen renforce la pression sur le prix du pétrole. Le baril de Brent de lamer du nord s'échange à 106$ ce lundi et le WTI américain à 102$. La fermeture de l'oléoduc représente une baisse de 4 millions de barils par jour et la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz en bloque 10 millions d'autres, poussant inexorablement l'or noir à la hausse.

france24fr.title: Macklemore écarté de la tournée d'Ed Sheeran après des propos pro-palestiniens
france24fr.description: Le rappeur américain Macklemore a été écarté de la tournée d’Ed Sheeran, a indiqué l’artiste lundi sur son compte Instagram. En cause, indique-t-il, sa prise de position pour la Palestine lors de ses concerts qui lui ont valu d'être considéré comme persona non grata par plusieurs salles de concert où il était attendu.

france24fr.title: "Comme percuté par un train" : le récit du pilote américain disparu en Iran, après son crash d'avion
france24fr.description: Le pilote américain dont l'avion s'est crashé en avril dernier en Iran s'est livré pour la première fois sur ce dramatique épisode et son périple de plus de 50 heures avant d'être finalement secouru par les forces spéciales.

france24fr.title: Cisjordanie occupée : à Masafer Yatta, les habitants démunis face aux destructions israéliennes
france24fr.description: Le 2 septembre, le village de Khirbet a-Taban en Cisjordanie occupée a été entièrement démoli par l’armée israélienne. Ce hameau est situé dans l'aire de Masafer Yatta, qu’Israël a définie comme une zone militaire. Il est le théâtre de tensions latentes avec des colons dont les habitants dénoncent le harcèlement.

france24fr.title: Kenya : des crocodiles deplacés parce qu'ils menacent les habitants
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, la forte concentration de crocodiles dans le lac Baringo représente une menace croissante pour les populations riveraines. Pour réduire les risques, les agents de la faune kényane capturent certains de ces reptiles avant de les transférer vers d’autres lacs du pays.

zeit.title: Sydney Sweeney: Sportlerinnen kritisieren sexualisierte Werbung mit Sydney Sweeney
zeit.description: Die US-Schauspielerin Sydney Sweeney wirbt mit Nacktfotos für einen Sportwettenanbieter. Die Werbekampagne löst unter Sportlerinnen eine heftige Kontroverse aus.

zeit.title: Autobranche: VW-Krise - Experte warnt vor Folgen für Personalgewinnung
Gala in Los Angeles: Comedy-Horror «Widow's Bay» erzielt Rekord bei Emmy-Gala
Sicherheit im Zugverkehr : Deutsche Bahn will Alkohol an allen Bahnhöfen verbieten
zeit.description: Nach dem gewaltsamen Tod eines Zugbegleiters sollen zahlreiche Maßnahmen für mehr Sicherheit sorgen. Unter anderem soll Alkoholkonsum an Bahnhöfen verboten werden.

zeit.title: Feuer: Stallbrand führt zu Millionenschaden - fünf Tiere sterben
Emmy Awards: »Widow’s Bay« und »The Pitt« sind die Sieger der Emmyverleihung
zeit.description: Die Horror-Comedyserie »Widow’s Bay« hat mehr Emmys gewonnen als jemals eine Serie in der Comedykategorie. »The Pitt« erhielt sechs Auszeichnungen.

zeit.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Staatssekretär: Europa droht bei KI zum Zuschauer zu werden
Nato-Ostflanke: Kampfflugzeuge schießen Drohne über Litauen ab
Social Media: Berlin-Wahl: Falsches Rathaus in Wahlwerbespot der Linken
Konjunktur: Chinas Wirtschaft lahmt - Konsum und Investitionen bremsen
Irankrieg: US-Kontrollbehörde beziffert bisherige Folgen des Irankriegs
zeit.description: Das US‑Verteidigungsministerium veröffentlicht erstmals eine Bilanz des Irankriegs. 17 US-Soldaten wurden getötet, Hunderte Gebäude zerstört und Flugzeuge beschädigt.

zeit.title: KI in der EU: USA bremsen bei KI – Europa will aufholen
zeit.description: Während KI-Unternehmen in den USA bremsen wollen, macht sich die EU bereit für die Aufholjagd. Kann das gut gehen? Und: Russland setzt weiter auf Eskalation.

zeit.title: Bill Gates: »Der Staat muss eingreifen«
zeit.description: Die Techbranche wird KI nicht selbst regulieren, sagt Bill Gates. Er warnt vor Jobverlusten und Bioterror. Und erklärt, was wir dringend von China lernen sollten.

zeit.title: Ursula Heinen-Esser: Was die Energiewende behindert? »Sehnsucht nach der guten alten Zeit!«
zeit.description: Sie muss die Energiewende vor der Bundesregierung schützen. Ursula Heinen-Esser ist die Cheflobbyistin für erneuerbare Energien in Berlin – und spürt Gegenwind.

nzz.title: Sydney Sweeney zeigt: Sex sells war gestern, heute verkauft sich Empörung. Selbst der Protest der Sportlerinnen gehört zum Kalkül
nzz.description: Die Schauspielerin posiert für den Sportwettenanbieter Novig fast nackt mit Sportutensilien. Moralische Fragen interessieren die Branche schon lange nicht mehr.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Kultur: «The Pitt» und «Widow’s Bay» triumphieren bei den Emmy Awards
KOMMENTAR - Häusliche Gewalt hat viel mit der Herkunft zu tun – es wird Zeit, dass die Behörden das Offensichtliche beim Namen nennen
nzz.description: Ausländische Männer sind gegenüber ihren Frauen und Kindern gewalttätiger als Schweizer. Das anzuerkennen, ist nicht fremdenfeindlich, sondern ein Schritt zur Bekämpfung des Problems.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Die Inflation wird für die Republikaner zu einem immer grösseren Problem
nzz.description: Donald Trump sagt, dass die USA für einen Sieg gegen Iran teureres Benzin in Kauf nehmen müssten. Das mag konsequent sein, könnte seine Partei in den Zwischenwahlen aber die Mehrheit kosten.

nzz.title: Mohammed bin Salmans jemenitischer Albtraum: Der Huthi-Vormarsch schockt Saudiarabien
nzz.description: Seit der Eroberung der Meerenge von Bab al-Mandab durch die Huthi kann das Königreich kaum mehr Erdöl exportieren. Welche Optionen hat der Kronprinz jetzt?

nzz.title: KI könnte zu gefährlich werden für die Menschheit, fürchten die Chefs der Techfirmen. Doch lässt sich KI überhaupt regulieren?
nzz.description: Die amerikanischen KI-Firmen wollen die technologische Entwicklung verlangsamen. Präsident Trump will das nicht. Wie könnte eine Regulierung aussehen?

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - «Die Marktschreier rufen die globale Krise aus – und dann passiert nichts», sagt der Präsident des Private-Equity-Riesen Blackstone
nzz.description: Blackstone gehört zu den grössten Investoren des KI-Booms. Jonathan Gray hält die Furcht vor einer Blase für unbegründet – und nimmt Stellung zur Nervosität unter Privatanlegern.

nzz.title: «Chaoten stoppen!» Luzern stimmt über schweizweit schärfstes Hooligan-Gesetz ab
nzz.description: Der Zentralschweizer Kanton wird zum Testfeld für den Schweizer Sport. Mit der Abstimmung über eine verpflichtende ID-Kontrolle beim Stadioneinlass erprobt Luzern die landesweit schärfste Massnahme gegen Fangewalt.

nzz.title: Die Schweiz gerät wegen der OECD-Mindeststeuer ins Hintertreffen. Zwei Professoren wollen Abhilfe schaffen
nzz.description: Für Grosskonzerne ist die Schweiz steuerlich weniger attraktiv geworden – besonders seit die USA aus der OECD-Mindeststeuer ausgestiegen sind. Doch es gibt Gegenmittel, wie ein neues Gutachten zeigt.

nzz.title: Claude Julien ist eine NHL-Ikone. Der neue ZSC-Coach weiss, dass in Zürich nur der Meistertitel gut genug ist
nzz.description: Die ZSC Lions starten als Favorit in die National-League-Saison – auch dank einem Kontingent von sieben Nationalspielern. Der im Sommer eingesetzte Coach Claude Julien soll das Team wie seine Vorgänger Marc Crawford und Bob Hartley zur Meisterschaft führen.

nzz.title: Finanzprüfer zerzausen Röstis Pläne für die Bahn und Strasse
nzz.description: Für die Finanzkontrolle ist nicht nachvollziehbar, wie der Bund die Ausbauprojekte priorisiert. Besonders scharf kritisieren sie den Grimseltunnel.

nzz.title: Politische Schlacht um die Burgen von Bellinzona
nzz.description: Bis heute ist das Wahrzeichen des Tessiner Kantonshauptortes kostenlos zugänglich. Die Gemeinde will für den Eintritt zu bestimmten Bereichen des Weltkulturerbes künftig Geld verlangen. Jetzt kommt es zur Volksabstimmung.

nzz.title: Der Pakt der Geächteten: Nordkorea und Russland giessen ihre Verbindung in Beton
nzz.description: Eine neue Autobrücke verbindet Nordkorea und Russland. Sie steht für eine Allianz, die aus der Not geboren ist und längst über Waffenlieferungen hinausgeht.

nzz.title: GASTKOMMENTAR - Erdogan gibt sich als Friedensfürst – doch kann ein Ausgleich mit den Kurden im Land ohne Demokratie gelingen?
nzz.description: Um seine Macht im Nahen Osten, aber auch in der Türkei zu festigen, plant Präsident Erdogan offensiv einen Ausgleich mit den Kurden im eigenen Land. Kann ein Frieden nach 42 Jahren Kampf tatsächlich gelingen, oder steht Erdogan sich selber im Weg?

nzz.title: Jordanien gerät ins Visier Irans – und wird gleichzeitig zum regionalen Handelsknotenpunkt
nzz.description: Jordanien wird seit einem halben Jahr zum Ziel iranischer Raketenangriffe. Obwohl die Tourismusbranche leidet, zeigt sich die jordanische Wirtschaft erstaunlich resilient – und könnte längerfristig vom Iran-Krieg profitieren.

nzz.title: In Kongo eskaliert die Lage um Ebola. An der nahen Grenze versucht Dr. Kalanzi, das Virus fernzuhalten. Doch die Menschen sagen: «Wir sterben hier eher an Hunger als an Ebola»
nzz.description: Uganda hat keine Ebola-Fälle. Das soll so bleiben. Doch da sind die laxen Spitalangestellten, die Hühnerschmuggler und die Kongolesen, die die Grenze öffnen wollen.

observador.title: Coreia do Norte promete apoio "inabalável" à Rússia
observador.description: Moscovo e Pyongyang concluíram um acordo de defesa em 2024 e milhares de soldados norte-coreanos participaram nos combates contra as forças ucranianas na região russa de Kursk. Israel ataca Gaza.

observador.title: O Castelo de Trancoso
observador.description: A história desta antiga fortificação, que inclui torre do séc. X, fala da campanha de Almansor, do castelo gótico do séc. XIII, da Feira, o uso em oitocentos e o restauro pelo Estado Novo.

observador.title: As notícias das 6h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: História de Ceuta desde que passou a ser espanhola
observador.description: Após o fim da dinastia filipina, Ceuta passou a ser espanhola, e assim continua até hoje. Que território é este, caso único de presença europeia na África continental após a era das descolonizações?

observador.title: Queijo na lancheira? Os dentes agradecem
observador.description: Pode uma fatia de queijo ajudar a proteger os dentes dos miúdos? Há ciência por trás desta surpresa da lancheira. A Nutricionista Mariana Chaves explica como.

observador.title: Medicamentos em casa: o que guardar e o que nunca usar
observador.description: Tem um armário cheio de medicamentos em casa? Mais do que ter muitos produtos, importa saber o que deve guardar, como conservar e o que nunca deve tomar por sua conta.

observador.title: Retratos "à francesa" pelo olhar de Manuel dos Santos
observador.description: Um dos três compositores franceses tem "ar de galã", diz Manuel dos Santos. Será Saint-Saëns, Debussy ou Saint-Georges? Revela ainda que guarda em casa perto de uma centena de obras da sua autoria.

observador.title: Inteligência artificial: o fim do mundo visto da China
observador.description: Depois dos alertas sobre os riscos da inteligência artificial, olhamos para a forma como a China pretende resolver o problema e, ao mesmo tempo, ganhar a corrida aos EUA.

observador.title: 4h. Dois incêndios lavram em Castelo Branco
observador.description: Mobilizam a esta hora mais de 800 bombeiros e 260 meios terrestres. Ainda, o diretor nacional da Polícia Judiciária está a ser investigado pela PJ por abuso de poder e falsas declarações em tribunal.

observador.title: 3h. IL não se posiciona sobre CPI ao ministro da Educação
observador.description: Mariana Leitão explica que não vai tomar uma decisão enquanto não ouvir esclarecimentos que já pediu. Ainda, o Ministério Público está a investigar o diretor nacional da Polícia Judiciária.

observador.title: 2h. Escolas alargam turmas para acomodar alunos sem vaga
observador.description: Diretores de agrupamentos de escolas de Lisboa, a Agência para a Gestão do Sistema Educativo e o MECI estiveram reunidos para resolver a questão. Ainda, incêndio lavram em Proença-a-Nova.

observador.title: 1h. Ministério Público investiga diretor nacional da PJ
observador.description: Em causa a alegada prática dos crimes de falsas declarações por ter referido no julgamento de Rui Pinto que não foram feitas escutas na investigação. Ainda, MEO foi alvo de um ataque em massa.

observador.title: Bruma deixa Benfica e assina com gregos do Aris Salónica
observador.description: Após passar grande parte da última época a recuperar de uma lesão grave, o extremo português deixa o clube da Luz pelo Aris Salónica, atual sétimo classificado na liga grega.

observador.title: Mais de 30 reclusos em greve de fome na Guiné-Bissau
observador.description: A greve de fome foi decretada, alegadamente, pela escassez de guardas prisionais no centro de reclusão de Bafatá. Como forma de denunciar a situação, mais de 30 reclusos iniciaram uma greve de fome.

observador.title: O dividendo orçamental de Montenegro
observador.description: O Governo está a baixar o IRS e, ao mesmo tempo, a distribuir suplementos extraordinários aos pensionistas. A combinação pode fazer sentido. Mas tem riscos.

observador.title: Quem tem medo de Passos Coelho?
observador.description: Tem medo de Passos Coelho quem, no fundo, não gosta de ver as suas próprias misérias expostas. Tem medo quem é pequeno. O país político e o país mediático estão recheados de gente pequena.

observador.title: "O tempo está a esgotar-se"
observador.description: Passos está a fazer um diagnóstico sobre os riscos que o PSD e o sistema político-partidário enfrentam. Se nada for feito, pode chegar o dia em que os partidos tradicionais darão lugar a outros.

observador.title: Vem aí a geração mais pé-rapada de sempre
observador.description: A verdade é que agora a escola serve para mais. Serve para as crianças aprenderem a ler, escrever e contar com alguém que no futuro as sustente, porque não vão ter habilitações para o fazerem sozinhas

spiegel.title: Tennis: Boris Becker fordert neue Regel wegen Alexander Zverevs Balltippen
spiegel.description: Alexander Zverevs zeitraubendes Ballauftippen vor seinen zweiten Aufschlägen hat bei den US Open nicht nur die Gegner verärgert. Auch Boris Becker möchte dies künftig unterbinden, hat aber auch viel Lob für den Weltranglistenzweiten übrig.

spiegel.title: New York: Warum Menschen in SoHo für ein 60-Dollar-Brot anstehen
spiegel.description: Mal eben mit etwas Kleingeld zum Bäcker gehen? Wer im New Yorker Viertel Soho bei »Rye« einkauft, sollte besser auch die Kreditkarte einstecken. Der österreichische Betreiber verteidigt den Preis für sein Brot aus Sauerteig.

spiegel.title: Nato registriert mehr hybride Angriffe von Russland
spiegel.description: Sabotage, Cyberattacken, Sprengstoffdrohnen: Russland intensiviert seine verdeckten Operationen gegen Nato-Staaten. Das Militärbündnis will jetzt gegensteuern und die Abschreckung erhöhen.

spiegel.title: Friedrich Merz: Führende CDU-Politiker stellen sich hinter den Kanzler
spiegel.description: In der Union wächst die Kritik an Friedrich Merz. Doch in der CDU gibt es auch andere Stimmen. Reformkanzler hätten es nie leicht, sagt Mittelstandsbeauftragte Gitta Connemann. Auch andere Christdemokraten signalisieren Unterstützung.

spiegel.title: Ernährung: Sind Linsenchips gesünder als Kartoffelchips?
spiegel.description: Weniger Fett, mehr Eiweiß: Knabbereien aus Hülsenfrüchten sind, so behaupten es die Hersteller, besser als die traditionelle Variante aus Kartoffeln. Ein Ernährungsmediziner ordnet das ein.

spiegel.title: »Watzmann ermittelt«: Was lernt man in der Krimi-Serie über Berchtesgaden?
News: Hohe Benzinpreise, Merz-Unterstützer in der CDU, Pistorius besucht Hegseth
spiegel.description: Das Tanken wird immer teurer, und schuld daran ist nicht nur Trump. Alle schreiben Merz ab, doch er hat auch noch Unterstützer bei der CDU. Und: Pistorius besucht Hegseth – und bringt ein verlockendes Angebot mit. Das ist die Lage am Dienstagmorgen.

spiegel.title: Muskeln aufbauen, Gewicht verlieren: Bodybuilder Urs Kalecinski erklärt, wie es wirklich klappt
spiegel.description: Der Bodybuilder Urs Kalecinski verrät, was viele Menschen beim Krafttraining falsch machen, wer von Protein- und Kreatinpulver profitiert. Und welche fünf Übungen das perfekte Training ergeben.

spiegel.title: Fitness: Den Blutzucker tracken, um die Leistung zu verbessern – bringt's das?
spiegel.description: Früher trugen vor allem Diabetiker einen Sensor für die Glukosemessung auf der Haut. Mittlerweile gilt er auch bei Kerngesunden als schick. Sie hoffen auf mehr Power beim Training und weniger Kilos.

spiegel.title: Emmys 2026: »The Pitt« als beste Dramaserie ausgezeichnet, »Widow's Bay« als beste Comedy
spiegel.description: Zweites Jahr, zweiter Sieg: Die Krankenhausserie »The Pitt« räumt bei der Verleihung des wichtigsten US-Fernsehpreises ab. Jean Smart und Matthew Rhys schreiben Emmy-Geschichte. Auch die Macher von »Widow’s Bay« haben Grund zur Freude.

spiegel.title: Künstliche Intelligenz: Elon Musk zieht Apple-Klage zurück, OpenAI-Verfahren läuft
spiegel.description: Sein Chatbot Grok sollte die Download-Charts bei Apple anführen, findet Elon Musk. Weil dem jedoch nicht so ist, witterte er Monopolisierung und bemühte die Richter. Jetzt macht er einen Rückzieher.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Supreme Court lässt Präsident im Streit um Briefwahl scheitern
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident will die Wahl per Post einschränken, scheitert damit aber nun auch vor dem Supreme Court. Ein anderes Verfahren lief für Donald Trump kaum besser. Und dann sind da noch die Umfragewerte.

spiegel.title: Russland-Ukraine-Krieg: Nato-Kampfjets schießen Drohne über Litauen ab
spiegel.description: Eine Drohne ist in den litauischen Luftraum eingedrungen – und abgeschossen worden. Präsident Nausėda bedankt sich bei der Nato und verweist auf »die zunehmende Aggression Russlands gegen die Ukraine«.

spiegel.title: Prinz Harry und Herzogin Meghan: Kinder wechseln in Großbritannien die Schule – nach zwei Tagen
spiegel.description: Prinz Archie und Prinzessin Lilibet sind gerade mit ihren Eltern aus den USA nach Großbritannien gezogen. An ihre neue Schule konnten sich die Kinder aber kaum gewöhnen. Zu groß waren offenbar die Sorgen um die Sicherheit der Familie.

spiegel.title: Modedesigner Bob Mackie ist tot: Er entwarf Outfits für Cher, Tina Turner und Marilyn Monroe
spiegel.description: Bob Mackie entwarf das legendäre »Happy Birthday, Mr. President«-Kleid für Marilyn Monroe, ver- und enthüllte Cher und Tina Turner: Nun ist der Modedesigner gestorben.

spiegel.title: Lützkampen, Rheinland-Pfalz: Motorradfahrer liegt 19 Stunden verletzt im Wald
spiegel.description: Ein 69 Jahre alter Mann hatte bei Lützkampen wohl eine Rechtskurve zu spät gesehen. Er kam mit seinem Motorrad von der Straße ab und landete verletzt in einem Wald. Nur durch Zufall wurde er am nächsten Tag gefunden.

spiegel.title: Ed Sheeran wirft Macklemore bei seiner Tour raus
spiegel.description: Rapper Macklemore trat auf Ed Sheerans Tour zweimal im Vorprogramm auf, nutzte die Bühne für »Free Palestine«-Rufe. Nun ist die Zusammenarbeit vorbei. Und der US-Rapper meint, er solle zum Schweigen gebracht werden.

spiegel.title: Hannover 96 trennt sich von Trainer Titz – übernimmt jetzt Sandro Wagner?

phys-org.title: Hidden receptor interactions may explain past failures of brain disorder drugs
phys-org.description: Metabotropic glutamate receptors, which are important but difficult drug targets, interact in surprisingly varied ways with their principal regulatory proteins, according to two new studies led by Weill Cornell Medicine investigators. undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: The People Not Worth Replacing
proj-syn.description: At first glance, MAGA’s fear of immigrants and the rest of America’s fear of data centers have many similarities, with each reflecting insecurities about one’s place in a changing economy. But while the first fear tells natives that their place is valuable, the second assumes that it will soon be worth nothing.

proj-syn.title: What Amodei’s Call for an AI Pause Gets Wrong
proj-syn.description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s recent appeal for a pause on AI development is a welcome one. But while AI companies do indeed need more breathing space to consider the full impact of their inventions before releasing them to the market, self-interested oversight is not the kind of governance we need.

proj-syn.title: The Strategic Asset Europe Has Overlooked
proj-syn.description: Europe’s soil is gradually dying, and yet the continent has still not recognized it as a strategic asset. Fortunately, the EU has many of the tools it needs to act, but doing so will require an overarching framework that helps farmers access financial rewards for measurable soil outcomes.

proj-syn.title: Who Is Responsible for Nepal’s Tragedy?
proj-syn.description: The devastating floods in Nepal demonstrate what happens when reckless development puts climate-vulnerable communities in harm’s way. They also highlight a climate-finance system that is unable to provide the funds countries need in the immediate aftermath of such disasters.

proj-syn.title: Europe Must Choose Between Power and Dependence
proj-syn.description: European citizens do not want “more Europe” in the abstract, but rather a European Union that is capable of protecting, investing, anticipating, deciding, and acting whenever national-level policymaking is insufficient. In today’s world, ensuring citizens’ control over their future requires the freedom to act together.

proj-syn.title: Progressive Economics Is Delivering
proj-syn.description: By combining fiscal responsibility, growth, and social development, progressive governments in Brazil and Spain have improved millions of people’s lives and refuted the hoary belief that conservatives are better stewards of the economy. Such a successful alternative model could not have come at a better time.

proj-syn.title: The Agentic Information Economy
proj-syn.description: An internet populated and run by AI agents will need not just reliable data but also a broader information ecology capable of questioning its own inputs and transmitting corrections where they are needed if information changes. But whether this will serve private interests or the public good remains to be seen.

proj-syn.title: Who Owns What AI Learns?
proj-syn.description: Since frontier AI models have already consumed much of the readily available stock of public knowledge on the internet, what remains is the valuable tacit knowledge embedded within organizations. Whoever sets the terms of how this knowledge is teased out and transferred will set the terms of the next economy.

proj-syn.title: America First Is Jeopardizing Taiwan’s Greatest Asset
proj-syn.description: Rather than strengthening Taiwan, US demands for market access, technology investment, and defense capabilities are deepening political polarization and eroding the island’s ability to build consensus just when it needs it most. The timing could hardly be worse.

proj-syn.title: Technology Is Not Above the Law
proj-syn.description: In arguing for a regulatory regime that is skewed entirely toward freeing developers to build online services, rather than placing any social obligations on them, the AI industry is using a playbook that Silicon Valley wrote 30 years ago. This time, however, the public seems less inclined to buy the industry's argument.

proj-syn.title: China’s Platform State and the AI Race
proj-syn.description: Balancing regulation with innovation is never easy, and the Chinese government’s robust support for AI could lead to inefficiency and excess. But the “platform state” model, combined with other strengths, has enabled China to achieve dominance in multiple strategic sectors, while enhancing its resilience.

proj-syn.title: Which Future for Online Life?
proj-syn.description: By articulating a vision of the future that seems inevitable, technology industry leaders want to create the impression that the surrender of privacy and other defining trends of the current moment cannot be stopped. But predictions become self-fulfilling prophecies only if we believe them and act accordingly.

proj-syn.title: When Words Are No Longer for Us
proj-syn.description: Owing to the proliferation of large language models throughout our software and social systems, we are now undergoing a textpocalypse, marked by not just a deluge of slop but a fundamental unmooring of language and text from lived human experience. The first victim is likely to be the internet itself.

proj-syn.title: Who Will Do the World’s “Most Impossible Job”?
proj-syn.description: Although the United Nations is facing a financial and political crisis that is almost certain to get worse before it gets better, the field of candidates vying for the organization’s top job is surprisingly crowded. If history is any guide, power politics, more than anything else, will decide the outcome.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Pro-Human Vision
proj-syn.description: The original vision of the internet as a democratizing force failed to account for the manner in which power would concentrate, attention would be monetized, and public discourse would be manipulated. In Europe and elsewhere, these lessons now must inform how we govern generative AI.

proj-syn.title: Superintelligent Democracy
proj-syn.description: Rather than framing the pursuit of AI capabilities as a race, we should turn the process into a democratic mission, with milestones set by the people, rather than on their behalf. Taiwan's own demonstration of mission-led governance, along with insights from the open-web community, show what is possible.

proj-syn.title: Will We Preserve the Sources of Human Learning?
proj-syn.description: By obscuring or destroying the primary sources of knowledge, large language models create the illusion of an embodied and active collection of everything we know. But without examining and interrogating the human originators of recorded knowledge and wisdom, one cannot fully develop one’s own understanding.

proj-syn.title: AI Is Fracking the Open Web
proj-syn.description: The demand for what digital publishers offer is real and robust, but the old methods of managing it will no longer work when cyberspace is inundated with bots designed to extract value wherever it can be found. Building an alternative will fall to the remaining advocates of the old open web.
